title: Why You Need a Licensed Architect for Your Home Addition in Westchester NY
excerpt: A home addition done right requires both design expertise and construction knowledge. That's why working with a design-build firm in Westchester makes all the difference.
content:
Adding space to your home is one of the biggest decisions you'll make as a homeowner. Whether you're looking to expand your kitchen, add a second story, or create a primary suite addition, the project will touch every system in your house. Electrical, plumbing, structural support, roofing, foundation work. Get it wrong and you're dealing with problems for years.

The smart move is to work with someone who understands both the design side and the construction side. That's what a design-build approach in Westchester gives you from day one.

What Makes Design-Build Different

Most homeowners hire an architect to draw plans, then hire a general contractor to build them. There's a problem with that setup. The architect isn't on site watching the work. The contractor isn't part of the design conversations. When reality hits, when walls come down and you see what's actually there, nobody has the full picture.

A design-build firm works differently. The same person who designs your addition is the one building it. Silvio M. Luca, principal of House Architecture & Construction, is a licensed architect in New York and a licensed general contractor. He runs every project personally. That means when decisions need to be made during construction, he's there to make them without anyone playing telephone between design and build.

Permit Processes Are Normal Across Westchester

Every town in Westchester County has its own building department. Whether you're in Scarsdale, Bronxville, Larchmont, or Mamaroneck, you'll go through a local permit process. This isn't unique to any one municipality. It's just how things work here.

What matters is having someone who knows how to work with these departments. A residential architect in Scarsdale or Pelham needs to understand local requirements, sight line restrictions, and what each building inspector expects. That knowledge saves time and prevents delays.

From Concept to Completion

Whether you're planning a kitchen remodel in White Plains, a bathroom renovation in Rye, or a full second-story addition in Tarrytown, the process is the same. You start with a real conversation about what you actually need. Not what looks good in a magazine, but how your family lives.

House Architecture & Construction serves all of Westchester County, from Eastchester to Ossining. The firm handles home additions in Westchester of all kinds. Additions, renovations, kitchen and bathroom work, primary suite expansions, historic restorations, open-concept conversions, and custom new construction. When your architect is also your general contractor, you get one point of accountability for the entire project.
